title: Introductions and Identity
summary: Names, origin, languages, and basic personal information.
whyItMatters: Introducing yourself is the first reusable situation in a new language. With a small set of identity words, you can give your name, origin, place of residence, and languages, then understand the same information from someone else.

mentalModel.title: Build a four-part identity card
mentalModel.content: Organize a basic introduction into four pieces: name, origin, residence, and languages. You can add or remove a piece depending on the situation.

mentalModel.title: Learn countries and languages as pairs
mentalModel.content: Connect the country with its language: Deutschland–Deutsch, Spanien–Spanisch, Italien–Italienisch. The forms are related but not always identical.

mentalModel.title: Separate origin from residence
mentalModel.content: 'Ich komme aus ...' says where you are from. 'Ich wohne in ...' says where you live now. They can name different places.

ruleBlocks.title: Give your name
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Ich heiße ...' or 'Mein Name ist ...'. In everyday introductions, 'Ich bin ...' is also common.

ruleBlocks.title: State your origin
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Ich komme aus ...' with a country or city: 'Ich komme aus Pakistan' or 'Ich komme aus Lahore.'

ruleBlocks.title: Say where you live
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Ich wohne in ...' with a city or place: 'Ich wohne in Berlin.'

ruleBlocks.title: Name the languages you speak
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Ich spreche ...' followed by a language: 'Ich spreche Urdu, Englisch und ein bisschen Deutsch.'

patterns: Ich komme aus + country or city
sentenceStructure: Keep one piece of personal information in each short sentence.
Use 'aus' for origin and 'in' for residence.
Join languages with 'und': 'Ich spreche Englisch und Deutsch.'
Use 'ein bisschen' before a language to express limited ability.

concepts: give a name, origin, residence, and languages
add family, occupation, and contact information
describe other people in simple terms
explain changes in residence, work, or language learning

comparisons.summary: The identity lesson supplies the personal information. The grammar lesson explains the verb forms used to express it, including 'ich heiße', 'ich komme', and 'ich spreche'.
The communication lesson turns this identity card into a two-way exchange by asking for each piece of information.

examples.de: Hallo, ich heiße Leila. Ich komme aus Marokko.
examples.en: Hello, my name is Leila. I come from Morocco.

examples.de: Ich komme aus Italien, aber ich wohne in Köln.
examples.en: I come from Italy, but I live in Cologne.

examples.de: Ich spreche Italienisch, Englisch und ein bisschen Deutsch.
examples.en: I speak Italian, English, and a little German.

examples.de: Mein Name ist Daniel. Ich bin neu hier.
examples.en: My name is Daniel. I am new here.

examples.de: Das ist Ana. Sie kommt aus Spanien und wohnt in München.
examples.en: This is Ana. She comes from Spain and lives in Munich.

commonMistakes.reason: Use 'aus' to express where someone comes from.
Use 'in' to state the place where someone lives.
'Deutschland' is the country; 'Deutsch' is the language.

specialCases: Most country names are used without an article after 'aus', but some countries use one, such as 'aus der Türkei'.
'Woher kommen Sie?' is formal; 'Woher kommst du?' is informal.
A person may choose not to share every part of the identity card. A name alone can be enough for a brief introduction.
tips: Write a four-sentence profile about yourself and practice it until the order feels flexible.
Create country-language pairs for the places most relevant to your life.
Practice one true profile and one fictional profile so you learn the pattern rather than one memorized answer.

memoryHooks.title: The four-line identity card
memoryHooks.content: Name, origin, residence, language: heiße, komme aus, wohne in, spreche.

memoryHooks.title: From uses aus; living uses in
memoryHooks.content: Picture movement out of your origin with 'aus' and your current location inside a place with 'in'.
